ACME Corporation — Building Access and Security

An access badge must be worn visibly at all times within company premises. Staff are expected to challenge politely, or report, any individual on site without a visible badge.
Visitors must be signed in at reception and escorted by their host at all times while on site. Visitors are issued a temporary badge that expires automatically at the end of the day.
Standard building access hours are 06:00 to 22:00, Monday to Friday. Badge access outside these hours is declined unless out-of-hours permission has been granted.
Out-of-hours and weekend access requires written approval from a department head, recorded in the access management system. Approval is granted for a defined period and expires automatically.
A lost or stolen access badge must be reported to the facilities team within 24 hours. The badge is deactivated on report and a replacement issued on verification of identity.

Tailgating, meaning allowing another person to follow through a controlled door on a single badge presentation, is prohibited. Each person must present their own badge at every controlled entry point.

ACME Corporation — Equipment Allocation and Return

Company laptops are refreshed on a 3-year cycle. Replacement outside the cycle is available where a device fails or where a documented technical requirement cannot be met by the existing specification.
Each workstation is allocated a maximum of 2 monitors as standard. Additional displays require a documented business justification approved by the department head and the IT team.
A one-off home office allowance of $300 is available to employees working remotely on a regular basis. The allowance covers desk, chair and lighting and is claimed through the expense system.

An ergonomic workstation assessment is available to any employee on request, conducted by the occupational health provider. Recommended equipment arising from an assessment is provided at company cost.
All company equipment must be returned within 5 working days of the final day of employment. Return is arranged through the facilities team, which issues a signed receipt for each item.
Where equipment is damaged through demonstrable negligence, an excess of $100 is recharged to the employee. Accidental damage and fair wear and tear are not recharged.

ACME Corporation — Workspace and Health and Safety

Desks must be booked at least 24 hours in advance through the workspace booking system. Unbooked desks may be released to other staff from 10:00 on the day.

Hot-desking operates in zones B and C. Zone A retains allocated seating for teams requiring fixed equipment or handling Restricted data.

Fire evacuation drills are conducted quarterly at each site. Participation is mandatory and attendance is recorded against the staff roll at the assembly point.
A minimum of 2 trained first aiders must be present on each occupied floor during working hours. Names and locations are displayed at every floor entrance and lift lobby.
All workplace accidents and near misses must be recorded in the incident log, regardless of whether injury occurred. Entries are reviewed monthly by the health and safety committee.
Food and drink other than water are prohibited in laboratory and server areas. Designated break areas are provided on each floor for consumption of food and hot drinks.

ACME Corporation — Corporate Card Policy

Corporate cards are issued to employees at manager grade and above, and to named staff with a demonstrable travel requirement. Applications are approved by the Finance Director.
The standard monthly spending limit on a corporate card is $5,000. Temporary limit increases may be granted for a defined period where a specific business need is evidenced in advance.

Personal use of a corporate card is prohibited without exception, including where the employee intends to repay the amount. Breach is treated as a disciplinary matter under the company conduct policy.

Cardholders must reconcile their statement and submit supporting receipts within 10 calendar days of the statement date. Unreconciled transactions are escalated to the cardholder's line manager after this point.

A lost or stolen corporate card must be reported to the card provider and to the finance team within 24 hours of discovery. The card is blocked immediately on report and a replacement issued within five working days.

Corporate card privileges are suspended following two recorded breaches of this policy within a rolling 12-month period. Reinstatement requires approval from the Finance Director and completion of refresher training.

ACME Corporation — Expense Claims and Approval

All expense claims must be approved by the claimant's line manager before processing. Managers may not approve their own expenses; these are routed to the next level of authority in the reporting chain.

Expense claims exceeding $500 require additional written approval from a company director. Claims are not released for payment until the director approval is recorded against the claim in the finance system.

Receipts supporting an expense claim must be submitted within 30 days of the date the expense was incurred. Claims submitted without supporting receipts after this window are rejected and may not be resubmitted.

Approved expense claims are reimbursed within 15 business days of final approval, paid by bank transfer to the account held on the employee record. Payment runs are processed each Tuesday and Thursday.

Business mileage in a private vehicle is reimbursed at $0.45 per mile for the first 10,000 miles in a tax year and $0.25 per mile thereafter. A journey log showing date, route and purpose must accompany the claim.

Alcohol is not a reimbursable expense under any circumstances, including where it forms part of a client entertainment bill. Itemised bills must separate alcohol from food, and only the food element is reimbursed.

ACME Corporation — Procurement Thresholds and Authority

Purchases with a total value below $1,000 require a single written quotation. The requesting department retains the quotation on file for audit purposes for a period of six years.

Purchases valued between $1,000 and $10,000 require three independent written quotations. Where three quotations cannot reasonably be obtained, a single-source justification must be approved by the Finance Director.

Any purchase with a total value above $10,000 must go through a formal tender process managed by the procurement team. The tender must be advertised for a minimum of 21 calendar days before evaluation begins.

Where a preferred supplier exists for a category of spend, that supplier must be used unless a documented exception is approved. The preferred supplier list is reviewed annually by the procurement team.

A purchase order must be raised and approved before any commitment is made to a supplier. Invoices received without a matching purchase order are held and returned to the originating department for regularisation.
Contracts with a total committed value above $50,000 may only be signed by the Chief Financial Officer or a delegate named in writing. Signature by any other party does not bind the company.

ACME Corporation — Annual Leave and Holiday Policy

Full-time employees accrue an annual leave entitlement of 25 working days per calendar year, exclusive of public holidays. Entitlement accrues monthly from the date of joining and is pro-rated for part-time staff according to contracted hours.

A maximum of 5 unused annual leave days may be carried over into the following calendar year. Carried-over days must be taken before 31 March or they are forfeited. Carry-over beyond this limit requires written approval from the Head of People.

Annual leave requests must be submitted at least 14 calendar days before the intended start date. Requests submitted with less notice may be refused at the discretion of the line manager, except in cases of bereavement or medical emergency.

A leave blackout period operates from 15 December to 5 January inclusive, during which annual leave is granted only where business cover can be demonstrated. Teams providing customer-facing cover are subject to an additional blackout during the final week of each quarter.

On termination of employment, accrued but untaken annual leave is paid as a pro-rata settlement in the final salary payment. Leave taken in excess of accrued entitlement is recovered from the final payment at the employee's daily rate.

Annual leave is approved by the employee's direct line manager. Absences exceeding 10 consecutive working days additionally require countersignature from the relevant department head before the request is confirmed.

ACME Corporation — Performance Review Cycle

Formal performance reviews are conducted twice per year, in March and September. Each review covers objectives set at the previous cycle, demonstrated behaviours, and development priorities for the period ahead.

Performance is assessed on a five-point rating scale, where 1 indicates performance significantly below expectation and 5 indicates performance consistently exceeding expectation. Ratings of 1 or 2 trigger a formal support conversation.

All proposed ratings are reviewed by a moderation committee chaired by the Head of People before publication. The committee ensures consistency of standard across departments and may require a manager to revisit a proposed rating.

An employee who disagrees with a published rating may appeal in writing within 10 working days of receiving it. Appeals are heard by a manager outside the employee's reporting line and the outcome is final.

Where sustained underperformance is identified, a Performance Improvement Plan is opened for a period of 90 days. The plan sets measurable objectives with fortnightly check-ins and a documented outcome at conclusion.

Employees become eligible for consideration for promotion after 12 months in their current role. Exceptional cases may be brought forward by a department head with written justification to the Head of People.

ACME Corporation — Probation and Notice Periods

New employees serve a standard probationary period of 6 months from their start date. During probation, performance is reviewed informally each month and formally at the midpoint and conclusion of the period.
A probationary period may be extended once by a maximum of 3 months where performance concerns have been documented and a development plan is in place. Further extension is not permitted.

During the probationary period, either party may terminate the employment relationship by giving 1 week of written notice. No reason is required, though the company will ordinarily set out its rationale in writing.
Following confirmation of appointment, the standard notice period is 1 calendar month for both the employee and the company. Notice must be given in writing and takes effect from the date of receipt.

Employees at senior management grade and above are subject to a 3-month notice period in both directions. This is specified in the individual contract of employment and supersedes the standard arrangement.

The company reserves the right to place an employee on garden leave for all or part of the notice period. Salary and contractual benefits continue during garden leave, but the employee may not attend the workplace or contact clients.

ACME Corporation — Device Security and BYOD

Full-disk encryption is mandatory on every device used to access company data, including laptops, desktops and removable storage. Devices failing an encryption check are blocked from the network.

Personal devices used for work must be enrolled in the company mobile device management platform before access is granted. Enrolment applies a security baseline and enables remote wipe of the work container only.
Operating system and security patches must be applied within 14 days of release. Devices more than 14 days behind on critical patches are placed in a restricted network segment until remediated.
Jailbroken, rooted or otherwise modified devices may not be used to access company data under any circumstances. Detection results in immediate revocation of access pending investigation.
On termination of employment, company data is remotely wiped from all enrolled devices on the final working day. For personal devices, only the managed work container is removed.
Devices must apply an automatic screen lock after 5 minutes of inactivity, requiring re-authentication to resume. This setting is enforced by policy and cannot be altered by the user.

ACME Corporation — Security Incident Reporting

A suspected security incident must be reported within 1 hour of discovery. Reporting is required even where the reporter is uncertain whether an incident has genuinely occurred.
Incidents are reported to the security team by email to the security reporting address or by the 24-hour incident hotline. Both channels are monitored continuously, including outside business hours.
Incidents are classified on a four-level severity scale from P1, denoting critical business impact or confirmed data loss, through to P4, denoting minor issues with no material impact.
A P1 incident receives an initial response within 30 minutes of being raised, at any hour. The on-call security engineer acknowledges the incident and convenes the response bridge.
A post-incident review is completed within 5 working days of incident closure. The review documents root cause, timeline, and remedial actions with named owners and target dates.

Employees must not disclose details of a security incident outside the company, including on social media, until the communications team has issued formal guidance. Enquiries from press are referred to the communications team.

ACME Corporation — Password and Authentication Policy

Account passwords must be a minimum of 14 characters in length. Complexity is achieved through length and unpredictability rather than mandatory character class mixing, in line with current guidance.
Passwords must be changed every 90 days. The system issues reminders at 14, 7 and 1 day before expiry, and access is suspended where a password is not changed by the expiry date.
Multi-factor authentication is mandatory for all remote access to company systems, including VPN, webmail and cloud administration consoles. Access attempts without a second factor are rejected.
All staff must store work credentials in the company-provided password manager. Storing credentials in browsers, spreadsheets, notes applications or physical documents is prohibited.
A new password may not match any of the previous 12 passwords used on the account. The system enforces this automatically and rejects reuse at the point of change.
An account is locked after 5 consecutive failed authentication attempts. Lockout persists for 30 minutes or until released by the service desk following identity verification.
